verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) qualifications as they relate to major alterations

## 0. Scope decision (stated up front because the request is ambiguous)

The request can be read two ways, and the regulation answers each with a different section:

- **(A) What must a person have to *hold* an IA?** — 14 CFR 65.91(c). The major-alteration element is built directly into the qualification: the required written test is on "returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations."
- **(B) What may an IA holder do *about* a major alteration?** — 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1), read with Part 43 (§§ 43.3(d), 43.5, 43.7, 43.9(d) and appendix B).

Both are answered below. All regulation text quoted is from eCFR (https://www.ecfr.gov/), fetched 2026-11-15T21:17:16Z; section hashes are recorded in §5 so a reviewer can confirm the same text.

---

## 1. Eligibility to hold an IA — 14 CFR 65.91(c) (verbatim, eCFR current)

> **§ 65.91 Inspection authorization.**
> (a) An application for an inspection authorization is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator.
> (b) An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization.
> (c) To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—
> (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;
> (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;
> (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;
> (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
> (5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.
>
> An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test.

### Qualification table (the five criteria and their exact thresholds)

| # | Requirement | Citation | Threshold / condition (as written) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mechanic certificate, both ratings | 65.91(c)(1) | Currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** airframe **and** powerplant ratings, each currently effective, **in effect for a total of at least 3 years** |
| 2 | Recent active engagement | 65.91(c)(2) | Actively engaged for **at least the 2-year period before the application date** in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR chapter I |
| 3 | Fixed base of operations | 65.91(c)(3) | A base where reachable **in person or by telephone during a normal working week**; need not be where the authority is exercised |
| 4 | Equipment, facilities, inspection data | 65.91(c)(4) | Equipment, facilities, and inspection data **necessary to properly inspect** airframes, powerplants, propellers, or related parts/appliances |
| 5 | Written test | 65.91(c)(5) | Pass a written test on ability to inspect per safety standards for **returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations** and annual and progressive inspections under Part 43 |
| — | Retest bar | 65.91(c), undesignated closing text | After a failure, may not reapply for retesting until **at least 90 days** after the failure date |
| — | Application mechanics | 65.91(a)–(b) | Apply on the form and in the manner prescribed by the Administrator; an applicant meeting the section is **entitled** to the authorization |

**Why this matters to "major alterations":** criterion (c)(5) is the direct link — the IA applicant is tested specifically on the safety standards for approving aircraft for return to service after major repairs and major alterations. The qualification is therefore not merely "A&P plus time"; it includes demonstrated competence in major-alteration return-to-service inspection.

**Adjacent sections not quoted here (verify on eCFR before use):** §§ 65.92 (duration) and 65.93 (renewal) sit immediately after § 65.91 and govern how the authorization stays valid. Their specific time periods and training/renewal thresholds are **not** among the excerpts this analysis is grounded on, so no figures are stated for them. Do not treat this document as authority on IA duration or renewal.

---

## 2. The IA's authority over major alterations — 14 CFR 65.95 (verbatim, eCFR current)

> **§ 65.95 Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations.**
> (a) The holder of an inspection authorization may—
> (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and
> (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter.
> (b) When he exercises the privileges of an inspection authorization the holder shall keep it available for inspection by the aircraft owner, the mechanic submitting the aircraft, repair, or alteration for approval (if any), and shall present it upon the request of the Administrator or an authorized representative of the National Transportation Safety Board, or of any Federal, State, or local law enforcement officer.
> (c) If the holder of an inspection authorization changes his fixed base of operation, he may not exercise the privileges of the authorization until he has notified the responsible Flight Standards office or International Field Office for the area in which the new base is located, in writing, of the change.

### Elements an IA must satisfy when signing off a major alteration

1. **Who** — the holder of an inspection authorization (65.95(a)(1)).
2. **What** — *inspect and approve for return to service* any aircraft or related part or appliance after a major repair or major alteration.
3. **Condition precedent** — the work **was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**. This is the operative gate: no approved technical data, no approval for return to service.
4. **Carve-out** — aircraft maintained under a **continuous airworthiness program under Part 121** are excluded from the 65.95(a)(1) privilege.
5. **Document custody** — the IA must keep the authorization available for the aircraft owner, the mechanic submitting the aircraft/repair/alteration for approval, and present it on request of the Administrator, an NTSB authorized representative, or any Federal, State, or local law enforcement officer (65.95(b)).
6. **Base change** — a change of fixed base of operations bars exercise of the privileges until **written** notice is given to the responsible Flight Standards office (or International Field Office) for the new base (65.95(c)).

---

## 3. Part 43 cross-requirements the IA must meet on a major alteration

- **§ 43.5 — Approval for return to service.** No person may approve for return to service an aircraft, airframe, engine, propeller, or appliance that has undergone maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration unless: (a) the maintenance record entry required by § 43.9 or § 43.11 has been made; (b) the repair or alteration form authorized by or furnished by the Administrator has been executed in the prescribed manner; and (c) if the repair or alteration changes the operating limitations or flight data in the approved aircraft flight manual, those limitations or data are appropriately revised per § 91.9. (All three are preconditions to the IA's signature, not optional paperwork.)
- **§ 43.7 — Who may approve for return to service.** Except as provided in that section and § 43.17, only the Administrator may approve for return to service; the holder of a mechanic certificate **or an inspection authorization** may approve as provided in Part 65; a repair station certificate holder may approve as provided in Part 145; a manufacturer may approve work it performed under § 43.3(j), and except for minor alterations that work must have been done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.
- **§ 43.3(d) — Supervision limit.** A person working under the supervision of a mechanic or repairman certificate holder may perform the maintenance, preventive maintenance, and alterations the supervisor is authorized to perform, but that paragraph **does not authorize any inspection required by Part 91 or Part 125, or any inspection performed after a major repair or alteration**. The post-major-alteration inspection is not delegable to an unsupervised helper.
- **§ 43.9(d) / appendix B to Part 43** — maintenance-record and major repair/alteration recordkeeping requirements (the repair-and-alteration form trail that § 43.5(b) depends on).
- **Part 43 applicability** — Part 43 does not apply to every aircraft; the eCFR text excludes, among others, aircraft for which the FAA issued an experimental airworthiness certificate (unless a different certificate was previously issued for that aircraft), certain light-sport aircraft previously certificated under § 21.190, and Part 107 operations except as described in § 107.140(d). Confirm applicability before asserting that the IA approval framework governs a given aircraft.

**Negative statement worth stating plainly:** an A&P mechanic who does **not** hold an IA is not the person who approves a major alteration for return to service under § 65.95(a)(1). Outside the IA route, major-alteration return-to-service approval runs through the Administrator, a Part 145 repair station, or a manufacturer under § 43.7(d)/§ 43.3(j).

---

## 4. Operating checklist for an IA holder approving a major alteration for return to service

1. **Confirm the article is within Part 43 and not the § 65.95(a)(1) carve-out.** If the aircraft is maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program, the IA privilege in § 65.95(a)(1) does not apply.
2. **Confirm the change is a major alteration** under the Part 1 definition. *(Provenance note: the Part 1 definition — an alteration not listed in the aircraft, engine, or propeller specifications that might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness, or that is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations — was **not** among the fetched eCFR excerpts for this analysis. Verify the exact wording at 14 CFR Part 1 before quoting it in a record or letter.)*
3. **Verify the technical data is approved by the Administrator** (STC, TC/production-certificate holder data, or other FAA-approved data). This is the § 65.95(a)(1) condition. *FAA advisory material (AC 43.13-2B, FAA Order 8900.1, the FAA-H-8083-30 AMT handbooks) explains what counts as approved versus acceptable data; that material is guidance, not regulation, and should be cited as such.*
4. **Inspect the work** against that approved data. The post-major-alteration inspection is not delegable under § 43.3(d).
5. **Confirm the maintenance record entry** required by § 43.9 (or § 43.11) has been made — § 43.5(a).
6. **Confirm the repair/alteration form** authorized or furnished by the Administrator has been executed in the prescribed manner — § 43.5(b) (for major repairs/alterations this is the FAA Form 337 trail; verify current form instructions in FAA guidance, not eCFR).
7. **Confirm operating-limitation/flight-manual changes** are revised per § 91.9 if the alteration changes them — § 43.5(c).
8. **Sign the approval for return to service** as the IA holder, and keep the authorization available as § 65.95(b) requires. If the IA's fixed base changed, give written notice to the responsible Flight Standards office first — § 65.95(c).

---

## 5. Source and currency statement (ask 2)

- **Primary source:** eCFR, https://www.ecfr.gov/ — accepted as a good source and used for every regulation quotation above. Sections used: 14 CFR 65.91 and 65.95 (Part 65, Subpart D); 14 CFR 43.3, 43.5, and the Part 43 page (including § 43.7 text and the Part 43 applicability exclusions).
- **Fetch record:** retrieved 2026-11-15T21:17:16Z. Section content hashes (sha256, first 12 hex): § 65.91 `8dd2b52b76db`; § 65.95 `04eedc455339`; Part 43 landing page `61a4f2b93dcb`; § 43.5 `d1da91fb4e54`; § 43.3 `b10f62b56b41`.
- **Currency caveat:** eCFR is the continuously updated electronic edition; the official publications are the annually printed CFR and the Federal Register. Before relying on this in a legal or enforcement-sensitive context, (i) check the eCFR "current as of" date and use the "Go to Date" feature, (ii) confirm no pending or recently effective amendments to §§ 65.91, 65.95, 43.3, 43.5, or 43.7, and (iii) note that eCFR carries regulations only — FAA Advisory Circulars, Order 8900.1, and the FAA-H-8083-30 AMT handbook series are advisory and are not on eCFR.
- **Not covered by this answer:** IA duration and renewal (§§ 65.92, 65.93) thresholds; the Part 1 definition of major alteration as verbatim text; operator-specific rules (Part 121/135), state or local requirements, or non-U.S. rules; and the FAA-AMT training-material treatment of this subject beyond the regulatory text.

---

## 6. One-line answer

To hold an inspection authorization a person must, under **14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)–(5)**, hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings each in effect for a total of at least 3 years, have been actively engaged for at least the 2 years before applying in maintaining aircraft under the chapter, have a fixed base of operations where reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week, have the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect, and pass a written test that expressly covers returning aircraft to service after **major repairs and major alterations** (with a 90-day bar on retesting after failure); and, having the authorization, the holder may under **14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)** inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part or appliance after a major repair or major alteration — except aircraft maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program — only if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator, with the Part 43 § 43.5 record/form/limitations preconditions satisfied.

verdict.summary:
QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) WITH RESPECT TO MAJOR ALTERATIONS — 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart E, read with Part 43

Source: eCFR (ecfr.gov), current text as fetched for this iteration: 14 CFR 65.91(c), 65.95, 65.85, 65.87, 43.5, and Part 43 appendices A and B. Where a section was not in the fetched set it is flagged explicitly below rather than asserted.

=====================================================================
0. HOW THE QUESTION RESOLVES
=====================================================================
The question as phrased covers two distinct regulatory questions, and both are answered because 'qualifications ... regarding major alterations' spans them:

  A. QUALIFICATIONS TO HOLD AN IA — 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)-(5). Five eligibility criteria. None of them is specific to alterations; they are the gate to the authorization itself.
  B. WHAT THE IA MAY DO ABOUT A MAJOR ALTERATION — 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1). This is the privilege, and it carries its own three conditions.

A person who holds neither an IA nor another approval authority listed in 43.5 may NOT approve a major alteration for return to service (see section 3). The IA is the mechanism by which a certificated mechanic acquires that authority.

=====================================================================
1. ELIGIBILITY — 14 CFR 65.91(c) (verbatim, as fetched)
=====================================================================
"(b) An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization.
 (c) To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—
  (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;
  (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;
  (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;
  (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
  (5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter."

Restated as a compliance checklist:

  C1. A&P BOTH RATINGS, 3 YEARS. A currently effective mechanic certificate carrying BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and each in effect for a total of at least 3 years. A single-rating (airframe-only or powerplant-only) certificate does not qualify. The 3-year clock runs on the ratings, not on the IA application date.
  C2. 2 YEARS ACTIVE ENGAGEMENT. Actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period immediately before the application date, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR Chapter I. This is a separate and shorter window than C1 and must not be conflated with it.
  C3. FIXED BASE OF OPERATIONS. A fixed base at which the holder can be reached in person or by telephone during a normal working week. It need not be the place where the IA privileges are exercised.
  C4. EQUIPMENT, FACILITIES, AND INSPECTION DATA. The equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or related parts/appliances must be available to the holder.
  C5. WRITTEN TEST. Pass a written test on ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after MAJOR REPAIRS AND MAJOR ALTERATIONS, and for annual and progressive inspections under Part 43. This is the one eligibility element that is expressly alteration-related: the test content is defined by reference to major repairs and major alterations.

Note on (a): the application form and manner provision of 65.91(a) was not in the fetched passage set; the form of application should be confirmed on the current eCFR text of 65.91(a) before relying on it procedurally. It does not affect the substantive criteria above.

=====================================================================
2. THE MAJOR-ALTERATION PRIVILEGE — 14 CFR 65.95 (verbatim, as fetched)
=====================================================================
"(a) The holder of an inspection authorization may—
  (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 of this chapter, if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator; and
  (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter.
 (b) When he exercises the privileges of an inspection authorization the holder shall keep it available for inspection by the aircraft owner, the mechanic submitting the aircraft, repair, or alteration for approval (if any), and shall present it upon the request of the Administrator or an authorized representative of the National Transportation Safety Board, or of any Federal, State, or local law enforcement officer.
 (c) If the holder of an inspection authorization changes his fixed base of operation, he may not exercise the privileges of the authorization until he has notified the responsible Flight Standards office or International Field Office for the area in which the new base is located, in writing, of the change."

Three conditions must all be satisfied before an IA holder signs off a major alteration under (a)(1):

  M1. SCOPE OF PRODUCT. It is an aircraft, or a related part or appliance — but NOT an aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under Part 121. Part 121 continuous-airworthiness aircraft are outside the IA's alteration-approval authority; approval flows through the operator's certificate (43.5(e)). The exclusion is written to Part 121 only; it does not by its terms exclude Part 135 aircraft, which approve under Part 135 per 43.5(e).
  M2. WORK DONE TO FAA-APPROVED TECHNICAL DATA. The major alteration must have been accomplished in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator. If the data is not FAA-approved, the IA has no basis to approve for return to service under (a)(1).
  M3. PART 43 COMPLIANCE. The alteration must be accomplished and recorded in accordance with Part 43.

Prerequisites to the act of approving for return to service, from 43.5 (verbatim, as fetched):
"No person may approve for return to service any aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, or appliance, that has undergone maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration unless—
 (a) The maintenance record entry required by § 43.9 or § 43.11, as appropriate, has been made;
 (b) The repair or alteration form authorized by or furnished by the Administrator has been executed in a manner prescribed by the Administrator; and
 (c) If a repair or an alteration results in any change in the aircraft operating limitations or flight data contained in the approved aircraft flight manual, those operating limitations or flight data are appropriately revised and set forth as prescribed by § 91.9 of this chapter."

So the IA's signature is the last step, not the only step: record entry (43.9/43.11), the FAA Form 337 (the repair/alteration form referenced in 43.5(b), with major alterations recorded per Appendix B to Part 43), and any AFM/operating-limitation revision under 43.5(c)/91.9 must already be in place.

Operating conditions attached to exercising the privilege:
  - 65.95(b): carry the authorization and keep it available to the owner, the submitting mechanic, and produce it on request of the FAA, NTSB, or federal/state/local law enforcement.
  - 65.95(c): on change of fixed base, the holder may not exercise IA privileges until written notice is given to the responsible Flight Standards office (or International Field Office) for the new area.

=====================================================================
3. THE NEGATIVE IMPLICATION — WHO CANNOT APPROVE A MAJOR ALTERATION
=====================================================================
This is the practical core of the question. A mechanic certificate alone does not carry major-alteration approval authority.

65.85(a) (verbatim, as fetched): "...a certificated mechanic with an airframe rating may approve for return to service an airframe, or any related part or appliance, after that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (EXCLUDING MAJOR REPAIRS AND MAJOR ALTERATIONS)."
65.87(a) is identical in structure for the powerplant rating and powerplant/propeller work, with the same exclusion.

Limited exception — light-sport special airworthiness certificate products NOT produced under FAA approval:
  65.85(b): an airframe-rated mechanic may approve for return to service an airframe or related part/appliance of an LSA-certificated aircraft after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration, provided the major repair/alteration was authorized by, and performed in accordance with instructions developed by, the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA.
  65.87(b): the same for a powerplant or propeller.
  Cross-reference: Part 43 applicability to LSA (43.1(d) as fetched) removes the 43.5(b)/43.9(d) form requirement for products not produced under FAA approval, and removes the Appendix B recording requirement for major repairs/alterations on such products.

Other approval paths for a major alteration, from 43.5:
  43.5(b): the holder of a mechanic certificate OR an inspection authorization, as provided in Part 65 (this is the IA route).
  43.5(c): a repair station certificate holder, as provided in Part 145.
  43.5(d): a manufacturer, for work it performed under 43.3(j) — but except for minor alterations, the work must have been done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator.
  43.5(e): a Part 121 or Part 135 air carrier/operating certificate holder, as provided in Part 121 or 135.
  Also 43.5 (as fetched, in the 43.3 context): an Aircraft Maintenance Engineer may not approve a major repair or major alteration; a Transport Canada-approved AMO (or its authorized employee) may approve a major repair or major alteration performed under that section if performed in accordance with FAA-approved technical data.

=====================================================================
4. RENEWAL / CURRENCY — FLAGGED, NOT VERIFIED IN THIS ITERATION
=====================================================================
The IA is time-limited and renewed under 14 CFR 65.92 (duration) and 65.93 (renewal). Neither section was in the fetched passage set for this iteration, so no renewal hour counts, inspection counts, or activity figures are asserted here. Anyone relying on this answer for a renewal determination must read 65.92 and 65.93 on ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-E before acting. The eligibility criteria in section 1 above are unaffected by that gap.

=====================================================================
5. DEFINITIONS AND RECORDING THAT BEAR ON 'MAJOR ALTERATION'
=====================================================================
  - Appendix A to Part 43 — 'Major Alterations, Major Repairs, and Preventive Maintenance' — is the regulatory list that determines whether a given alteration is major. The major/minor determination is the threshold question; the IA privilege in 65.95(a)(1) attaches only to major repairs and major alterations.
  - Appendix B to Part 43 governs recording of major repairs and major alterations (the Form 337 route referenced by 43.5(b)).
  - Part 43 applicability carve-outs for experimental and LSA aircraft are in 43.1 (as fetched): 43.1(b) excludes certain experimental aircraft and Part 107 aircraft; 43.1(d) addresses LSA with the exceptions noted in section 3.

=====================================================================
6. ONE-PAGE COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST FOR AN IA HOLDER APPROVING A MAJOR ALTERATION
=====================================================================
Before signing:
  [ ] 1. Confirm the article is an aircraft, airframe, engine, propeller, appliance, or component part — and is NOT an aircraft maintained under a Part 121 continuous airworthiness program (65.95(a)(1)). If Part 121, stop; approval runs through the operator's certificate (43.5(e)).
  [ ] 2. Confirm the alteration is 'major' under Appendix A to Part 43. If minor, the IA privilege is not the operative authority; 65.85(a)/65.87(a) mechanic approval applies (subject to their exclusions).
  [ ] 3. Confirm the alteration was accomplished in accordance with technical data APPROVED BY THE ADMINISTRATOR (65.95(a)(1)). Unapproved data is disqualifying.
  [ ] 4. Confirm the 43.9/43.11 maintenance record entry has been made (43.5(a)).
  [ ] 5. Confirm the repair/alteration form (FAA Form 337) has been executed as prescribed (43.5(b); Appendix B to Part 43).
  [ ] 6. Confirm any resulting change to operating limitations or AFM flight data has been revised per 91.9 (43.5(c)).
  [ ] 7. Confirm the IA itself is current and that the fixed base of operations on record is correct; if the base changed, written notice to the responsible Flight Standards office must precede exercise of privileges (65.95(c)).
  [ ] 8. Keep the authorization available and produce it on request (65.95(b)).

=====================================================================
7. CAVEATS
=====================================================================
  - Text quoted is the eCFR 'current' version as fetched for this iteration. Confirm currency on ecfr.gov before relying on it for an enforcement-sensitive determination.
  - Sections 65.91(a) (application form), 65.92 (duration), 65.93 (renewal), and 65.94/65.96 (if present in the current subpart) were not among the fetched passages and are not characterized above beyond being flagged.
  - This answer is a regulatory reading, not a legal opinion and not FAA legal interpretation; advisory material (e.g., AC 43-9, AC 43.13-2, the IA practical-test standards) is outside the cited regulatory text and is not relied on here.

verdict.summary:
QUALIFICATIONS FOR AN INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) AS THEY RELATE TO MAJOR ALTERATIONS

GOVERNING SOURCE AND CURRENCY
Source: 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D (Inspection Authorization), eCFR 'current' text as retrieved 2026-11-15T21:20:44Z.
- 14 CFR 65.91 (sha256 8dd2b52b76db)
- 14 CFR 65.93 (sha256 d50ca977ec87)
- 14 CFR Part 65 Subpart D page, containing 65.91, 65.92, 65.93 (sha256 1dc594967131)
The retrieved text carries amendment history through Amdt. 65-65, 89 FR 80053 (Oct. 1, 2024). Regulations are amended; re-verify the eCFR revision date before relying on this in a certification action.

1. SHORT ANSWER
Exactly one IA qualification is specifically about major alterations: 14 CFR 65.91(c)(5). An IA applicant must pass a written test on his or her ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations, and after annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43. Major alterations appear a second time, as a renewal/currency option, in 65.93(a)(2). No other IA eligibility item in Part 65 is alteration-specific.

Quoted, 65.91(c)(5): 'Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.'

2. COMPLETE ELIGIBILITY SET - 14 CFR 65.91(c)
All five items must be met; the major-alteration link is item (5).

| Item | Requirement (regulation text, condensed) | Relation to major alterations |
|---|---|---|
| 65.91(c)(1) | Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and in effect for a total of at least 3 years | None directly; establishes the A&P base on which the IA rating is added |
| 65.91(c)(2) | Actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before application, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR Chapter I | None directly; that work is where major-alteration exposure is normally accumulated |
| 65.91(c)(3) | Fixed base of operations at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week; need not be where authority is exercised | None |
| 65.91(c)(4) | Equipment, facilities, and inspection data available to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance | Indirect: 'inspection data' is what an alteration approval is checked against |
| 65.91(c)(5) | Pass a written test on ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections under Part 43 | DIRECT - this is the major-alteration qualification |

Supporting rules in the same section:
- 65.91(a): application is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator. (The regulation does not name the form number; the IA application is commonly filed on FAA Form 8610-1 - confirm the current form with the responsible Flight Standards office.)
- 65.91(b): an applicant who meets the requirements of the section is entitled to the inspection authorization (entitlement language, not discretionary issuance).
- Retest bar (undesignated paragraph following 65.91(c)(5)): 'An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test.' The 90-day clock runs from the date of failure.

3. THE MAJOR-ALTERATION ELEMENT IN DETAIL
3.1 What the qualification actually is. It is a knowledge qualification evidenced by a written test, not an experience-count qualification. Part 65 imposes no minimum number of major alterations that an applicant must have performed or inspected before taking the IA test. The 3-year and 2-year figures in (c)(1) and (c)(2) are certificate-currency and active-engagement thresholds, not alteration counts.
3.2 What the test covers, per the regulation's own words. (a) Safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs; (b) safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major alterations; (c) annual inspections under Part 43; (d) progressive inspections under Part 43. Items (a) and (b) are the alteration-relevant content.
3.3 Definitional dependency. 'Major alteration' in 65.91(c)(5) takes its meaning from the Part 1 definition (14 CFR 1.1) and the alteration categories listed in Part 43, Appendix A. That classification drives whether a given task falls inside the (c)(5) test content and inside the 65.93(a)(2) currency option. CAUTION: the 14 CFR 1.1 definition text and the Part 43 Appendix A text were not present in the passages retrieved for this answer; the citations are correct, but quote the definition from eCFR directly before using it in a determination.
3.4 No separate rating. There is no 'major alteration' endorsement, stamp, or type-specific IA rating in Part 65. The IA is a single authorization added to a mechanic certificate; alteration scope is governed by the privileges rules (see section 6), not by qualification subcategories.

4. DURATION AND CONTINUING QUALIFICATION - 14 CFR 65.92
- 65.92(a): each inspection authorization expires on March 31 of each odd-numbered year; the holder may exercise privileges only while holding a currently effective mechanic certificate with both a currently effective airframe rating and a currently effective powerplant rating.
- 65.92(b): the authorization ceases to be effective whenever (1) it is surrendered, suspended, or revoked; (2) the holder no longer has a fixed base of operation; or (3) the holder no longer has the equipment, facilities, and inspection data required by 65.91(c)(3) and (4).
- 65.92(c): on the Administrator's request, a suspended or revoked authorization must be returned.

5. RENEWAL AND CURRENCY - 14 CFR 65.93 (where major alterations reappear)
5.1 Baseline. To renew for a 2-year period, the applicant must present evidence during March of each odd-numbered year at the responsible Flight Standards office that he or she still meets 65.91(c)(1) through (4). In addition, the applicant must show completion of one of the activities in 65.93(a)(1)-(5) by March 31 of the first year of the 2-year period, and completion of one of the five activities during the second year.
5.2 The five activities (65.93(a)):
 (1) performed at least one annual inspection for each 90 days the current authority was held; or
 (2) performed at least two major repairs or major alterations for each 90 days the current authority was held; or
 (3) performed, or supervised and approved, at least one progressive inspection per Administrator-prescribed standards; or
 (4) attended and successfully completed a refresher course acceptable to the Administrator of not less than 8 hours of instruction; or
 (5) passed an oral test by an FAA inspector to determine that knowledge of applicable regulations and standards is current.
5.3 Arithmetic for the major-alteration option, 65.93(a)(2). The unit is 'per 90 days held,' so the count scales with holding time. Using complete 90-day intervals (conservative reading; a partial interval is not counted as a full interval here):

| Period the authority was held | Days | Complete 90-day intervals | Minimum major repairs/alterations at 2 per interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| One 12-month year | 365 | 4 (365/90 = 4.06) | 8 |
| Full 2-year IA period | 730 | 8 (730/90 = 8.11) | 16 |
| Minimum stated unit (90 days) | 90 | 1 | 2 |

Note on interpretation: 65.93(a) requires an activity to be shown by March 31 of the first year and again during the second year, so in practice the (a)(2) count is demonstrated per year (about 8) and cumulatively over the authorization (about 16). Whether the FAA credits a partial 90-day interval is not resolved by the regulation text; the conservative planning number is the floor shown above. FAA Order 8900.1 guidance would resolve it, but that is outside the eCFR scope requested.
5.4 Grace provisions (65.93(b)). An IA holder whose authorization has been in effect (1) for less than 90 days before the expiration date need not comply with (a)(1)-(5); (2) for less than 90 days before March 31 of an even-numbered year need not comply with (a)(1)-(5) for the first year of the 2-year period.
5.5 Lapse consequence (65.93(c)). A holder who does not complete one of the (a)(1)-(5) activities by March 31 of the first year may not exercise IA privileges after that March 31. Privileges resume after passing an oral test by an FAA inspector on current regulations and standards; passing that oral test is deemed to satisfy the (a)(1)-(5) requirement by the first-year deadline.
5.6 Expired authorizations (65.93(d)). A person qualifying for relief under 14 CFR 61.40 is eligible to renew an expired inspection authorization under this section, provided the 61.40 requirements are met.

6. PRIVILEGE SIDE - CONTEXT ONLY, NOT A QUALIFICATION
Eligibility (section 2) is distinct from what the IA holder may approve. The privilege provision for major alterations is 14 CFR 65.95, which addresses inspecting and approving for return to service aircraft or related parts/appliances after a major repair or major alteration when the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator, with a carve-out for aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program. IMPORTANT: 65.95 text was NOT in the retrieved passage set for this answer. The citation is correct, but the precise scope and the continuous-airworthiness carve-out must be quoted from eCFR before being applied. Do not treat section 6 as verified regulatory text.

7. COMPLIANCE PROCEDURE - APPLYING THIS TO A CANDIDATE OR HOLDER
Step 1. Classify the task: major or minor alteration, using 14 CFR 1.1 and Part 43 Appendix A. Quote both from eCFR at the time of the determination.
Step 2. For an applicant: verify 65.91(c)(1) A&P with both ratings currently effective and in effect at least 3 years total; 65.91(c)(2) active engagement for the 2 years preceding application; 65.91(c)(3) fixed base with in-person or telephone reachability during a normal working week; 65.91(c)(4) equipment, facilities, and inspection data; 65.91(c)(5) written test passed, with the major-repair/major-alteration return-to-service content as the alteration-specific element.
Step 3. Record the test date. If failed, no reapplication before 90 days after the failure date (65.91(c)(5) trailing paragraph).
Step 4. For a holder: calendar the March 31 first-year and second-year activity deadlines; select one of 65.93(a)(1)-(5), using the (a)(2) count from the table in 5.3 if the major-alteration option is chosen; retain evidence of each event (the regulation requires the applicant to 'show' completion).
Step 5. Calendar the March-of-odd-year renewal presentation at the responsible Flight Standards office, including evidence of continued compliance with 65.91(c)(1)-(4).
Step 6. Monitor the 65.92(b) cessation triggers: loss of fixed base, loss of equipment/facilities/inspection data, or lapse of either the airframe or powerplant rating - any one ends the effectiveness of the authorization independent of the March 31 expiration date.
Step 7. If the first-year activity deadline is missed, stop exercising IA privileges after March 31 of the first year until the FAA oral test under 65.93(c) is passed.

8. WHAT PART 65 DOES NOT REQUIRE (common misconceptions)
- No minimum number of major alterations performed before obtaining the IA.
- No separate major-alteration endorsement or type rating.
- No additional practical/oral exam for initial issuance beyond the written test specified in 65.91(c)(5).
- No requirement that the fixed base be the place where authority is exercised (65.91(c)(3) says so expressly).
- No aircraft-category carve-out in 65.91 itself; the category limits, if any, arise in the privileges rule (65.95), which is outside the verified text for this answer.

9. OPEN ITEMS TO VERIFY BEFORE RELIANCE
(a) eCFR revision date at the time of use.
(b) 14 CFR 1.1 definition of 'major alteration' and Part 43 Appendix A alteration categories - not in the retrieved passages.
(c) 14 CFR 65.95 privileges text, including the continuous-airworthiness exception - not in the retrieved passages.
(d) Current application form number referenced by 65.91(a) - the regulation does not state it.
(e) FAA interpretation of 'for each 90 days' for partial intervals in 65.93(a)(2) - guidance, not regulation.

verdict.summary:
# Inspection Authorization (IA) qualifications as they relate to major alterations

**Answer identifier: 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)–(5)**, read with **14 CFR 65.91(c)(5)** (the IA written test is specifically a test on returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations) and **14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)** (the privilege those qualifications unlock). Source: eCFR, Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter D, Part 65, Subpart D.

---

## 1. Scope note (read this first)

The question as written — "qualifications for inspection authorization regarding major alterations" — sits at the junction of two different regulatory questions. Both are answered below, but they are not the same question:

| Question | Governing section |
|---|---|
| What must I have/do to **get** an IA? | §65.91 (eligibility) |
| What may an IA holder **do** with major alterations once certificated? | §65.95(a)(1) (privileges and limitations) |
| Who defines what counts as a **major** alteration? | Part 43, Appendix A (see §6 caveat) |

If your question is only "how do I qualify for the IA," §65.91(c) is the complete answer. The major-alteration content enters §65.91 only at **(c)(5)**, the written test.

---

## 2. The qualifications — verbatim, §65.91

> **§ 65.91 Inspection authorization.**
>
> (a) An application for an inspection authorization is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator.
>
> (b) An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization.
>
> (c) To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—
>
> (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;
>
> (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;
>
> (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;
>
> (4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
>
> (5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.
>
> An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test.
>
> [Docket 1179, 27 FR 7973, Aug. 10, 1962, as amended by Amdt. 65-5, 31 FR 3337, Mar. 3, 1966; Amdt. 65-22, 42 FR 46279, Sept. 15, 1977; Amdt. 65-30, 50 FR 15700, Apr. 19, 1985]

*Source: https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91 (fetched 2026-11-15, sha256 8dd2b52b76db).*

### 2.1 Plain-language restatement of each element

| ¶ | Requirement | Practical meaning | Failure mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) | Application on the form and in the manner the Administrator prescribes | Application is made to the FAA (currently via FAA Form 8610-1 — confirm the current form number at read time, as forms are revised outside the CFR) | Application not accepted |
| (c)(1) | Mechanic certificate with **both** airframe **and** powerplant ratings, each currently effective, each in effect for a **total of at least 3 years** | You cannot hold an IA on an airframe-only or powerplant-only certificate. Both ratings, and the 3-year clock runs on the ratings being in effect | Ineligible — no waiver exists in the rule text |
| (c)(2) | **Actively engaged** for **at least the 2-year period before applying** in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained under 14 CFR | The 2-year period immediately precedes the application date; it is a recency requirement, not a lifetime total | Ineligible |
| (c)(3) | A **fixed base of operations** where you can be reached in person or by telephone during a normal working week — need not be where you exercise IA privileges | Address of record; drives FSDO notification duty under §65.95(c) if it changes | Cannot exercise privileges until fixed |
| (c)(4) | Equipment, facilities, and **inspection data** available to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or related parts/appliances | This is the resource prong; "inspection data" here is what makes the §65.95(a)(1) approved-data determination possible | Cannot exercise privileges |
| (c)(5) | Pass the **written test** on ability to inspect per safety standards for returning aircraft to service after **major repairs and major alterations** and annual/progressive inspections under Part 43 | This is the only place §65.91 itself reaches major alterations: the test content is explicitly major-repair/major-alteration centric | Fail; retest barred for at least **90 days** |

**The 90-day bar** applies only to an applicant who *fails* the (c)(5) test. It is measured from the date of failure, not the date of application or notification.

---

## 3. Where "major alterations" actually binds the IA — §65.95(a)(1)

The qualifications in §65.91 exist to support the privilege in §65.95:

> **§ 65.95 Inspection authorization: Privileges and limitations.**
>
> (a) The holder of an inspection authorization may—
>
> (1) Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 [New] of this chapter, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**; and
>
> (2) Perform an annual, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection according to §§ 43.13 and 43.15 of this chapter.
>
> (b) When he exercises the privileges of an inspection authorization the holder shall keep it available for inspection by the aircraft owner, the mechanic submitting the aircraft, repair, or alteration for approval (if any), and shall present it upon the request of the Administrator or an authorized representative of the National Transportation Safety Board, or of any Federal, State, or local law enforcement officer.
>
> (c) If the holder of an inspection authorization changes his fixed base of operation, he may not exercise the privileges of the authorization until he has notified the responsible Flight Standards office or International Field Office for the area in which the new base is located, in writing, of the change.

*Source: https://ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.95 (fetched 2026-11-15, sha256 04eedc455339).*

### 3.1 Four conditions buried in §65.95(a)(1) — the exam traps

1. **Approved data, not acceptable data.** The alteration must have been done in accordance with *technical data approved by the Administrator*. An IA approving a major alteration performed on acceptable data (e.g., AC 43.13-1B generic practices) is outside the privilege. The qualification to hold the IA does not itself supply the approved-data authority — the data package does.
2. **Part 121 carve-out.** The privilege does not extend to aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program under Part 121.
3. **Personal performance.** Per the FAA's IA information guide, "The holder of an IA must personally perform the inspection. The regulations do not provide for delegation of this responsibility." *Source: https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/ia_info_guide.pdf.*
4. **Compatibility with prior work.** Same guide: during inspection of major repairs or alterations, the IA must also determine that they are compatible with previous repairs and alterations made to the aircraft.

### 3.2 Currency of the privilege (not the certificate)

- The authorization must be **kept available for inspection** by the owner, the submitting mechanic, the Administrator, NTSB representatives, and Federal/State/local law enforcement (§65.95(b)).
- **Change of fixed base:** privileges are suspended until written notice reaches the responsible Flight Standards office / International Field Office for the new area (§65.95(c)). This is the operational consequence of the §65.91(c)(3) qualification.

---

## 4. The baseline an IA is measured against — what an A&P alone may NOT do

The reason the IA question matters at all is that a plain mechanic certificate stops short of major alterations:

> **§ 65.85 Airframe rating; additional privileges.** (a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, a certificated mechanic with an airframe rating may approve for return to service an airframe, or any related part or appliance, after that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (**excluding major repairs and major alterations**). In addition, a certificated mechanic with an airframe rating may perform the 100-hour inspection required by part 91 …
>
> (b) A certificated mechanic with an airframe rating can approve for return to service an airframe, or any related part or appliance, of an aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration for products that are not produced under an FAA approval provided the major repair or major alteration was authorized by, and performed in accordance with instructions developed by, the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA.
>
> [Docket FAA-2023-1377, Amdt. No. 65-66, 90 FR 35218, July 24, 2025]

> **§ 65.87 Powerplant rating; additional privileges.** (a) … after that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (**excluding major repairs and major alterations**). … (b) [light-sport carve-out in parallel to §65.85(b)]

*Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65 (fetched 2026-11-15, sha256 ba0b5fa97a92).*

**Consequence:** the general rule is that approving a major alteration for return to service is an IA act, not an A&P act. The **exception** is the narrow light-sport path added by Amdt. 65-66 (90 FR 35218, July 24, 2025): an A&P with the matching rating may approve a major repair/alteration on a light-sport aircraft for products not produced under an FAA approval, where the work was authorized by and performed per instructions from the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA. Cite the amendment date when teaching this — many older study guides predate it and will mark the light-sport carve-out wrong.

---

## 5. Applicant checklist (usable as a pre-application audit)

| # | Check | Cite | Evidence to hold |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mechanic certificate currently effective | 65.91(c)(1) | Certificate |
| 2 | Airframe rating currently effective, in effect ≥ 3 years total | 65.91(c)(1) | Certificate issue date |
| 3 | Powerplant rating currently effective, in effect ≥ 3 years total | 65.91(c)(1) | Certificate issue date |
| 4 | Actively engaged in maintaining 14 CFR–certificated/maintained aircraft for ≥ the 2 years before application | 65.91(c)(2) | Employment/work records, logbooks, employer letters |
| 5 | Fixed base of operations with in-person or telephone reachability during a normal working week | 65.91(c)(3) | Address of record |
| 6 | Equipment, facilities, and inspection data available | 65.91(c)(4) | Tooling list, technical data library/subscriptions |
| 7 | Pass the IA written test (major repairs, major alterations, annual and progressive inspections under Part 43) | 65.91(c)(5) | Test report |
| 8 | If previously failed the test: ≥ 90 days elapsed since failure date | 65.91(c)(5) flush text | Test report date |

Note that items 1–3 are three distinct conditions: the certificate must be effective, **each** rating must be effective, and each rating must have been **in effect for a total of at least 3 years**. Do not collapse these into "held an A&P for 3 years."

---

## 6. Explicit verification gaps in this answer

Stated plainly so a downstream reviewer does not treat these as verified:

1. **Part 43, Appendix A** (the actual definition/enumeration of major alterations, by airframe/powerplant/propeller/appliance) was **not** among the fetched passages. It is the controlling definition for whether a given change is major, and it should be quoted from eCFR before being used in a compliance decision or in test prep. Do not substitute memory for it.
2. **§65.92 (duration) and §65.93 (renewal)** were not fetched. Their current text — including the duration period and the renewal evidence requirements — must be read from eCFR at time of use. No duration or renewal figure is asserted in this answer.
3. **The application form number** is not in the regulation text; §65.91(a) delegates it to the Administrator. Confirm the current form on faa.gov before filing.
4. **§43.9 / §43.11 recordkeeping** for the approval for return to service is referenced functionally above but not quoted; verify at eCFR if the answer is being used for a records-compliance question.

---

## 7. How to re-verify at read time

1. Open `https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91` and `.../section-65.95`.
2. Confirm the "current" date shown matches your intended effective date; eCFR exposes point-in-time versions if you need a historical revision.
3. Compare against the source notes above: §65.91 carries amendments through Amdt. 65-30 (50 FR 15700, Apr. 19, 1985); §65.95 through Docket FAA-2018-0119, Amdt. 65-57A, 83 FR 9171, Mar. 5, 2018. A different amendment line means the text moved — re-read, do not reuse this answer.
4. Cite as: `14 C.F.R. § 65.91(c)` and `14 C.F.R. § 65.95(a)(1)` (current through [date read]).

---

## 8. Exam-oriented one-liner (FAA-AMT context)

The IA qualification that is *about* major alterations is **§65.91(c)(5)**: the written test covers inspection according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations. The authority that qualification grants is **§65.95(a)(1)**: approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration, Part 121 aircraft excepted, only where the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator — and the IA must personally perform that inspection.

verdict.summary:
QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) WITH RESPECT TO MAJOR ALTERATIONS — 14 CFR (eCFR), FAA-AMT / A&P context

SCOPE AND ASSUMPTIONS (stated, not hidden)
- Jurisdiction: U.S. federal, 14 CFR as published on eCFR.
- 'FAA-AMT' read as the FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician (A&P certificate holder) context.
- 'Inspection auth' read as Inspection Authorization under 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D (§§65.91–65.95), because that is the only authorization that carries major-alteration approval authority for a mechanic.
- Aircraft category: general aviation / Part 91 unless the operator falls under Part 121, 135, or a Part 145 repair station (those approve under their own parts — see §43.7(c),(e)).

SHORT ANSWER
There is no separate 'major alteration' rating. There is exactly one authorization — the Inspection Authorization — and it is issued on a single set of eligibility criteria in 14 CFR §65.91(c). Only one of those five criteria mentions major alterations at all: the written test in §65.91(c)(5) must cover returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations. The authority to actually approve a major alteration for return to service then flows from holding the IA, per §43.7(b) and (the privilege itself) §65.95(a).

1. THE QUALIFICATIONS — 14 CFR §65.91(c)(1)–(5) (verbatim, fetched from eCFR)

(c)(1) Certificate and 3-year currency:
  'Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years'
  → Both ratings (A and P) required. Each rating must currently be effective AND have been in effect for a total of at least 3 years. The 3 years attaches to the ratings on the mechanic certificate, not to any prior IA or to employment.

(c)(2) Recent active engagement — 2 years:
  'Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter'
  → A 2-year look-back window immediately preceding application. Note this is a shorter window than the 3-year certificate requirement in (c)(1); the two are distinct tests and both must be met.

(c)(3) Fixed base of operations:
  'Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority'
  → Reachability, not the inspection workplace. Phone contact during a normal working week is expressly sufficient.

(c)(4) Equipment, facilities, and data:
  'Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance'
  → 'Inspection data' availability is the operational hook for major alterations: an IA cannot approve an alteration without the current approved technical data for it.

(c)(5) Written test — the only major-alteration-specific qualification:
  'Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.'
  → The IA exam is, by regulation, an examination on approving return to service after MAJOR REPAIRS and MAJOR ALTERATIONS, plus annual/progressive inspections. This is the sole place where major alterations appear as a qualification element.

Retest bar (same section, flush text after (c)(5)):
  'An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test.'
  → 90-day wait applies only to failure of the (c)(5) written test.

Application mechanics, §65.91(a)–(b): application is made 'on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator'; an applicant who meets the requirements of the section 'is entitled to an inspection authorization' (i.e., issuance is ministerial once the criteria are met).

2. WHAT THE IA MAY THEN DO WITH A MAJOR ALTERATION
- 14 CFR §43.7(a): 'Except as provided in this section and §43.17, no person, other than the Administrator, may approve an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part for return to service after it has undergone maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration.'
- 14 CFR §43.7(b): 'The holder of a mechanic certificate or an inspection authorization may approve ... for return to service as provided in Part 65 of this chapter.' → the mechanic/IA route; Part 65 then gates which of the two may approve a major alteration.
- 14 CFR §65.95(a) — IA privileges (NOT re-fetched in this pass; verify text before citing in a compliance document): the IA holder may inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft or related part/appliance after a major repair or major alteration 'in accordance with Part 43' where the work was done 'in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator', excluding aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program. Treat this paragraph as the operative privilege and confirm against eCFR.
- Alternative approvers for a major alteration under §43.7: (c) repair station certificate holder under Part 145; (d) a manufacturer for work it performed under §43.3(j), where 'except for minor alterations, the work must have been done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator'; (e) Part 121/135 certificate holder under those parts; or (a) the Administrator.

3. THE NEGATIVE RULE THAT MOST OFTEN TRIPS PEOPLE UP — AN A&P ALONE CANNOT APPROVE A MAJOR ALTERATION
14 CFR §65.85(a) (verbatim): a certificated mechanic with an airframe rating 'may approve for return to service an airframe, or any related part or appliance, after that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (excluding major repairs and major alterations).'
→ Major repairs and major alterations are expressly carved out of ordinary A&P return-to-service authority. The single exception is §65.85(b): for an aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category, an airframe-rated mechanic may approve after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration 'for products that are not produced under an FAA approval provided the major repair or major alteration was authorized by, and performed in accordance with instructions developed by, the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA.'

4. DATA AND RECORD CONDITIONS THAT ATTACH TO ANY MAJOR-ALTERATION APPROVAL
- Approved data is a precondition, not a formality (§43.7(d) phrasing; AC 43.13-2C §10.4.2: major alterations 'will require completion of the FAA Form 337 ... using approved data').
- §43.9(a): the person who alters must make a record containing (1) a description or reference to data acceptable to the Administrator of work performed; (2) date of completion; (3) name of person performing the work if other than the approver; (4) 'the signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate held by the person approving the work. The signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed.'
- §43.9(d): 'In addition to the entry required by paragraph (a) of this section, major repairs and major alterations shall be entered on a form, and the form disposed of, in the manner prescribed in appendix B, by the person performing the work.' (Appendix B = FAA Form 337, Major Repair and Alteration.)
- §43.13(a)/(b): work must use the current manufacturer's maintenance manual or Instructions for Continued Airworthiness or other methods acceptable to the Administrator, with the required tools/equipment, and must leave the article 'at least equal to its original or properly altered condition.'

5. GUIDANCE LAYER (advisory, not regulatory) — AC 43.13-2C
Field-approval workflow for a major alteration, as written in AC 43.13-2C: submit FAA Form 337 prepared per Part 43, AC 43-210 and AC 43.9-1, including certification basis, description and ICA; 'The alteration must be performed by a certificated airframe mechanic, and accomplished using acceptable methods, techniques, and practices. Refer to 14 CFR §§43.7 and 43.13'; then 'The holder of an Inspection Authorization (IA) should inspect the aircraft for: Previous alterations or repairs that may not have been recorded. Compatibility of previous alterations or repairs. Airworthiness of the aircraft.' Also enumerated: STC, field approval by a trained and certificated FAA airworthiness ASI, or DER data on Form 8110-3 as the acceptable routes to approved data. Label all of this as guidance; it does not create or enlarge the §65.91 qualifications.

6. ONE-PAGE COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST DERIVED FROM THE ABOVE
[ ] Mechanic certificate currently effective with both Airframe and Powerplant ratings.
[ ] Each rating in effect a total of at least 3 years at time of application (§65.91(c)(1)).
[ ] Actively engaged in maintaining chapter-certificated aircraft throughout the 2 years immediately before application (§65.91(c)(2)).
[ ] Fixed base of operations, reachable in person or by telephone during a normal working week (§65.91(c)(3)).
[ ] Equipment, facilities, and current inspection data available (§65.91(c)(4)).
[ ] Written test passed, including return to service after major repairs and major alterations (§65.91(c)(5)); if failed, 90-day wait before retesting.
[ ] For the specific alteration: approved technical data in hand (STC / field approval / DER 8110-3 / other Administrator-approved data).
[ ] Form 337 completed and disposed of per Part 43 Appendix B; §43.9(a) log entry with signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate.
[ ] Aircraft weight and balance re-established if the alteration affects it (AC 43.13-2C step 6, citing §§43.13, 91.9, 91.103).

7. TEXT CURRENCY AND VERIFICATION LIST (be honest about what was and was not re-read)
