# Qualifications for Inspection Authorization (IA) With Respect to Major Alterations

Authority: 14 CFR (eCFR, Title 14). Context: FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician (AMT) / mechanic certificate holder under Part 65 Subpart D.

## 0. Bottom line

There is **no standalone 'major alteration' qualification**. The qualification is the **Inspection Authorization** itself, issued under **14 CFR 65.91**, and the major-alteration authority is a **privilege of that authorization** under **14 CFR 65.95(a)(1)**. An AMT holding only a mechanic certificate with airframe and/or powerplant ratings **cannot** approve a major alteration for return to service — 14 CFR 65.85 and 65.87(a) exclude major repairs and major alterations from the mechanic's return-to-service privilege.

Qualification chain, in order:

1. Hold a currently effective **mechanic certificate with both Airframe and Powerplant ratings**, in effect for a total of at least **3 years** — 65.91.
2. Have been **actively engaged** in maintenance / preventive maintenance / alteration of aircraft for at least **2 of the 3 years** immediately preceding application — 65.91.
3. Have a **fixed base of operations** — 65.91.
4. **Pass the FAA written (knowledge) test** for inspection authorization — 65.91.
5. Maintain mechanic **recent experience**: at least **6 months** of qualifying activity within the **preceding 24 months** — 65.83 (quoted below).
6. Renew every **2 years** (expires **31 March of odd-numbered years**) with evidence under 65.93, one option for which is *performing major repairs or major alterations*.

## 1. Scope and provenance legend

The request is ambiguous in one respect that changes the answer, so both readings are answered:

- **Reading A — 'what must an AMT do to be qualified to inspect/approve major alterations?'** → the IA eligibility requirements (§ 3, § 4).
- **Reading B — 'what qualification must the person who approves a major alteration for return to service hold?'** → § 4 and § 5 (43.7(b) + 65.95(a)(1)).

Provenance tags used throughout:

- **[QUOTED]** — text fetched from eCFR during research; safe to rely on as written.
- **[RECALLED — verify]** — provision is identified by cite and summarized from the regulation's substance, but its verbatim text was **not** in the fetched passage set. Re-read the cite on eCFR before filing this in a compliance record.

## 2. Table 1 — Qualification matrix

| # | Requirement | Cite | Applies to | Provenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mechanic certificate, Airframe + Powerplant, both currently effective | 65.71, 65.77, 65.91 | IA applicant | [RECALLED — verify] |
| 2 | A&P ratings in effect a total of ≥ 3 years | 65.91 | IA applicant | [RECALLED — verify] |
| 3 | Actively engaged in maintenance/preventive maintenance/alteration ≥ 2 of preceding 3 years | 65.91 | IA applicant | [RECALLED — verify] |
| 4 | Fixed base of operations | 65.91 | IA applicant | [RECALLED — verify] |
| 5 | Pass FAA written test | 65.91 | IA applicant | [RECALLED — verify] |
| 6 | 6 months qualifying activity in preceding 24 months | 65.83 | Any mechanic exercising privileges | [QUOTED] |
| 7 | May approve major alteration for RTS only per Administrator-approved technical data | 65.95(a)(1); 43.7(b) | IA holder | 43.7(b) [QUOTED]; 65.95 [RECALLED — verify] |
| 8 | Mechanic without IA may **not** approve major repair/alteration for RTS | 65.85; 65.87(a) | A&P only | 65.87(a) [QUOTED] |
| 9 | LSA limited exception for powerplant-rated mechanic | 65.87(b) | A&P only, LSA | [QUOTED] |
| 10 | Form 337 entry/disposition for major repairs & alterations | 43.9(d); appendix B to part 43 | Person performing work | 43.9(d) [QUOTED] |
| 11 | Operator must list current major alterations/repairs | 91.417(a)(2)(vi) | Owner/operator | [QUOTED] |

## 3. Prerequisite: the mechanic (AMT) certificate

The IA is **not** a certificate or rating; it is an authorization layered on top of an A&P mechanic certificate. The applicant must already hold a mechanic certificate with **both** airframe and powerplant ratings, and those ratings must have been in effect for a total of **3 years** before application. Practical consequence: an AMT with only an airframe rating, or with A&P held less than 3 years, is not eligible regardless of experience. **[RECALLED — verify against § 65.91(c)]**

Recent-experience gate for exercising any mechanic privilege (including the experience credited toward IA eligibility):

> "§ 65.83 Recent experience requirements. A certificated mechanic may not exercise the privileges of his certificate and rating unless, within the preceding 24 months— (a) The Administrator has found that he is able to do that work; or (b) He has, for at least 6 months— (1) Served as a mechanic under his certificate and rating; (2) Technically supervised other mechanics; (3) Supervised, in an executive capacity, the maintenance or alteration of aircraft; or (4) Been engaged in any combination of paragraph (b)(1), (2), or (3) of this section." **[QUOTED — eCFR § 65.83]**

Note the two different clocks and do not conflate them: **6 months / 24 months** (65.83, mechanic currency) versus **2 years / 3 years** (65.91, IA eligibility).

## 4. IA eligibility — 14 CFR 65.91

Substance of § 65.91 as applied to an AMT seeking major-alteration authority **[RECALLED — verify]**:

- (a) Application is made on the form and in the manner prescribed by the Administrator (FAA Form 8610-1).
- (b) An applicant who meets the requirements of the section is **entitled** to the authorization.
- (c) Eligibility:
  - (1) currently effective mechanic certificate with **both** airframe and powerplant ratings, each currently effective and **in effect a total of at least 3 years**;
  - (2) **actively engaged** in the maintenance, preventive maintenance, or alteration of aircraft for at least **2 of the 3 years** immediately preceding the date of application;
  - (3) a **fixed base of operations**;
  - (4) the remaining eligibility elements of the paragraph (including the **written test** and the equipment/facilities/inspection-data availability element).

Compliance note: 'actively engaged' is the element most often failed in an enforcement/audit review — it must be evidenced (employer letters, work orders, 8610-1 blocks, logbook entries), not merely asserted. The fixed-base element is what makes the holder locatable for FAA surveillance.

## 5. The major-alteration privilege and its limits

**Who may approve.** 43.7(b) **[QUOTED]**:

> "(b) The holder of a mechanic certificate or an inspection authorization may approve an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part for return to service as provided in Part 65 of this chapter."

43.7(b) is a pass-through; **Part 65 decides the scope**. For major alterations, Part 65 gives that approval power only to the **IA holder**.

**The IA privilege.** § 65.95(a)(1) **[RECALLED — verify]**: the holder of an inspection authorization may inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance **after a major repair or major alteration**, in accordance with Part 43, **if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator**. The same section excludes aircraft maintained under a continuous airworthiness maintenance program (see §§ 121.367 and 135.411(a)(2)) — those approvals flow through the operator's program, not the individual IA.

**Two hard conditions on every major-alteration approval by an IA:**

1. The alteration must be **major** as determined under the definitional framework in § 7 below (and if it is minor, no IA is needed — an A&P may approve it under 65.85/65.87(a)).
2. The work must have been accomplished under **technical data approved by the Administrator** (e.g., STC, FAA-approved design data, field approval where applicable). An IA may **not** approve for return to service a major alteration accomplished on unapproved data — this is the single most common substantive violation in this area.

## 6. Who may NOT approve a major alteration

**A&P mechanic without IA — barred.** § 65.87(a) **[QUOTED]**:

> "(a) Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, a certificated mechanic with a powerplant rating may approve for return to service a powerplant or propeller or any related part or appliance, after that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (**excluding major repairs and major alterations**)."

The identical exclusion appears in § 65.85 for airframe-rated mechanics **[RECALLED — verify]**. A mechanic may *perform* a major alteration (Part 43 § 43.3) but may not *approve it for return to service* without an IA or another 43.7 authority.

**Light-sport limited exception.** § 65.87(b) **[QUOTED]**: a powerplant-rated mechanic may approve for return to service a powerplant/propeller or related part/appliance of an aircraft with a **special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category** after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration **for products not produced under an FAA approval**, provided the alteration was authorized by, and performed per instructions developed by, the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA. This is narrow; it does not generalize to standard-category aircraft.

**Other 43.7 authorities** (for completeness, not IA qualifications): repair station (43.7(c), Part 145); manufacturer (43.7(d) — except for minor alterations, work must be done per Administrator-approved technical data); Part 121/135 certificate holders (43.7(e)); LSA repairman with maintenance rating (43.7(g)).

## 7. What counts as a 'major alteration'

Because the IA privilege is triggered by the major/minor line, the qualification question cannot be answered without the classification test:

- **14 CFR 1.1 definition** **[RECALLED — verify]**: a major alteration is an alteration not listed in the aircraft, aircraft engine, or propeller specifications that (1) might appreciably affect weight, balance, structural strength, performance, powerplant operation, flight characteristics, or other qualities affecting airworthiness; or (2) is not done according to accepted practices or cannot be done by elementary operations.
- **Appendix A to Part 43** lists major alterations and major repairs by system (airframe, powerplant, propeller, appliance) and also lists preventive maintenance. **[RECALLED — verify; the appendix was in the source list but no passage from it was captured]**
- FAA Order 8300.16 / Field Approval guidance is supplementary only; it does not create or remove the Part 65 qualification requirement.

## 8. Records the IA's approval generates

§ 43.9(a) **[QUOTED]** requires a maintenance-record entry with description/reference to acceptable data, date of completion, name of person performing the work if other than the approver, and the **signature, certificate number, and kind of certificate** of the person approving the work — and "[t]he signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed."

§ 43.9(d) **[QUOTED]**: "In addition to the entry required by paragraph (a) of this section, major repairs and major alterations shall be entered on a form, and the form disposed of, in the manner prescribed in appendix B, by the person performing the work." (That form is FAA Form 337.)

§ 91.417(a)(2)(vi) **[QUOTED]**: the owner/operator must keep "[a] list of current major alterations and repairs to each airframe, engine, propeller, rotor, and appliance."

## 9. Keeping the IA valid — and how major alterations feed renewal

- **Duration — § 65.92 [RECALLED — verify]:** each inspection authorization **expires 31 March of each odd-numbered year**; the holder may exercise privileges only while holding a currently effective mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings currently effective.
- **Renewal — § 65.93 [RECALLED — verify]:** to renew for a 2-year period, the holder must present evidence **on or before 31 March** of the applicable odd-numbered year that, during the preceding 12 months, at least one of the following occurred:
  1. performed at least one **annual inspection** for each 90 days the authorization was held; or
  2. performed at least **two major repairs or major alterations** for each 90 days the authorization was held; or
  3. performed or supervised and approved at least one **progressive inspection** per Administrator-prescribed standards; or
  4. attended and successfully completed a **refresher course** acceptable to the Administrator of **not less than 8 hours** of instruction; or
  5. passed an **oral test** by an FAA inspector to establish currency of knowledge.

  *Illustrative arithmetic (verify against FAA renewal guidance before relying on it): a full 12-month lookback contains four 90-day periods, so option (1) ≈ 4 annual inspections and option (2) ≈ 8 major repairs/alterations.* There is also a short-term-holder relief provision in 65.93(b) for authorizations in effect less than 90 days before the 31 March date.

This is the direct link the request is reaching for: **major alterations are both the object of the IA privilege (65.95) and one of the ways an IA stays current (65.93(a)(2)).**

## 10. Verification worksheet (do this before relying on the brief)

| Cite | What to confirm on eCFR | Why |
|---|---|---|
| § 65.91(c) | Exact paragraph letters and the '2 of the 3 years' / 'fixed base' / 'written test' wording | Not in fetched passage set |
| § 65.95 | Full text of (a) and (b), including the CAMP exclusion cites | Not in fetched passage set |
| § 65.85 | 'excluding major repairs and major alterations' wording | Analog to quoted 65.87(a) |
| § 65.92, § 65.93 | Expiration date, renewal options, 8-hour figure | Not in fetched passage set |
| § 1.1; appendix A to part 43 | Major-alteration definition and listed alterations | Not in fetched passage set |
| Currency | § 65.87 carries Amdt. 65-66, 90 FR 35219 (July 24, 2025) — confirm no later amendment to 65.91/65.93/65.95 | The one dated amendment captured is 2025 |

## 11. Audit checks that fall out of this brief

1. Approver held a **currently effective IA** on the date of approval (not just an A&P).
2. Approver's IA had not lapsed on 31 March of the odd-numbered year.
3. Approver satisfied 65.83 currency (6 months in preceding 24).
4. Alteration was correctly classified **major** (Part 1.1 / appendix A) — a misclassified major alteration approved by an A&P alone is an airworthiness violation even if the work was flawless.
5. Work was accomplished under **Administrator-approved technical data** (65.95(a)(1)).
6. FAA Form 337 executed and disposed per appendix B (43.9(d)); maintenance record entry per 43.9(a); operator's major-alteration list per 91.417(a)(2)(vi).
7. Aircraft not maintained under a CAMP to which the individual IA's approval does not extend (121.367 / 135.411(a)(2)).

## 12. Out of scope / not answered here

- Required Inspection Item (RII) programs under Parts 121/135 — a separate operator-program qualification, not an IA qualification.
- Field-approval procedure mechanics (Order 8300.16, AC 43-210A) — procedural, supplementary.
- Any non-US authority.

*Prepared as a written compliance deliverable; no repository or tooling was used or required. The [RECALLED — verify] items in § 10 must be re-read on eCFR before this brief is filed as a record of compliance.*

verdict.summary:
QUALIFICATIONS FOR AN INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) AS THEY RELATE TO MAJOR ALTERATIONS
Governing source: 14 CFR (eCFR), Part 65 Subpart D; Part 43. Text as retrieved 2026-11-15 from ecfr.gov and faa.gov (sha256 prefixes 8dd2b52b76db, 1dc594967131, f177d9ffff23, a78ad2ef1f32, ece24efe31ea).

=====================================================================
0. SCOPE NOTE — TWO QUESTIONS HIDE IN THIS ONE
=====================================================================
'Qualifications ... regarding major alterations' can mean either:
  (A) What must an applicant satisfy to BE ISSUED an IA — the eligibility criteria, and the fact that the written test is specifically about major repairs/major alterations? -> 14 CFR § 65.91(c).
  (B) What must be true of the IA HOLDER (privilege + limitation) to inspect and approve a major alteration for return to service? -> 14 CFR § 65.95(a)(1).
Both are answered below. They are different rules and exam questions frequently mix them.

On 'FAA-AMT': AMT = Aviation Maintenance Technician. Nothing in the AMT context (including Part 147, which certifies AMT *schools*, not individuals) changes the IA rule. Part 147 is not an IA-qualification pathway; the only pathway is Part 65 Subpart D. An IA is also not a 'rating' printed on the mechanic certificate — it is a separate authorization issued under Part 65 Subpart D.

=====================================================================
1. ELIGIBILITY TO OBTAIN AN IA — 14 CFR § 65.91
=====================================================================
§ 65.91(a): 'An application for an inspection authorization is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator.'
§ 65.91(b): 'An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization.' (i.e., meeting the criteria is entitlement, not a discretionary award.)

§ 65.91(c) — ALL FIVE must be met:

| # | Requirement (verbatim substance) | Evidence to have ready |
|---|----------------------------------|------------------------|
| (c)(1) | Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and each having been in effect for a total of at least 3 years | A&P mechanic certificate, both ratings current, with issue dates supporting 3 years in effect for each rating |
| (c)(2) | Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the application date, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR | Employment/engagement record, logbook or employer letters covering the 2 years immediately preceding application |
| (c)(3) | Have a fixed base of operations at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week — it need NOT be the place where the inspection authority is exercised | Address/phone of the fixed base declared on the application |
| (c)(4) | Have available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance | List of tooling, facilities, and current inspection data (maintenance manuals, ADs, approved data sources) at that base |
| (c)(5) | Pass a written test on ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after MAJOR REPAIRS and MAJOR ALTERATIONS, and annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43 | Test result / passing score from the Administrator |

Retest bar (§ 65.91(c), undesignated closing sentence): 'An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test.'

Note on (c)(5): the major-alteration content is baked directly into the IA knowledge test — the test is specifically on returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations, plus annual and progressive inspections under Part 43. This is the direct link between 'IA qualifications' and 'major alterations.'

=====================================================================
2. WHAT THE IA MAY DO WITH A MAJOR ALTERATION — 14 CFR § 65.95
=====================================================================
§ 65.95(a)(1): the IA may 'Inspect and approve for return to service any aircraft or related part or appliance (except any aircraft maintained in accordance with a continuous airworthiness program under part 121 of this chapter) after a major repair or major alteration to it in accordance with part 43 of this chapter, IF THE WORK WAS DONE IN ACCORDANCE WITH TECHNICAL DATA APPROVED BY THE ADMINISTRATOR.'
§ 65.95(a)(2): may perform an annual inspection, or perform or supervise a progressive inspection, per §§ 43.13 and 43.15.
§ 65.95(b): when exercising IA privileges the holder shall keep the authorization available for inspection by the aircraft owner and by the mechanic submitting the aircraft/repair/alteration for approval, and shall present it on request of the Administrator, an authorized NTSB representative, or any Federal, State, or local law enforcement officer.

Supporting provisions:
- § 43.7(b): 'The holder of a mechanic certificate or an inspection authorization may approve an aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, appliance, or component part for return to service as provided in Part 65 of this chapter.' (Part 65 is where the IA's major-alteration authority actually lives.)
- § 43.9(d): 'In addition to the entry required by paragraph (a) of this section, major repairs and major alterations shall be entered on a form, and the form disposed of, in the manner prescribed in appendix B, by the person performing the work.' (The IA's approval signature is a separate act from the performer's Appendix B entry.)
- § 65.85(a) — the CONTRAST that makes the IA necessary: a mechanic with only an airframe rating 'may approve for return to service an airframe, or any related part or appliance, after that person has performed, supervised, or inspected its maintenance or alteration (EXCLUDING MAJOR REPAIRS AND MAJOR ALTERATIONS).' § 65.85(b) carves out a narrow light-sport exception. So: a plain A&P cannot sign off a major alteration; an IA can.

=====================================================================
3. THE FOUR LIMITATIONS MOST OFTEN MISSED (from FAA IA Information Guide, Change 1, July 19, 2024)
=====================================================================
1. The IA CANNOT approve the data for a major repair or major alteration. The IA inspects to see that the alteration conforms to data PREVIOUSLY approved by the Administrator. Availability of approved data 'should be made prior to beginning the repair or alteration.'
2. The IA must PERSONALLY perform the inspection. 'The regulations do not provide for delegation of this responsibility.'
3. The IA must also determine the alteration is COMPATIBLE with previous repairs and alterations on the aircraft.
4. Part 121 continuous airworthiness program aircraft are excluded from the § 65.95(a)(1) approval privilege.
Related data-approval guidance named by the FAA guide: FAA Order 8300.16 (as revised), 'Major Repair, Alteration, and Data Approval,' plus FAA field approval job aids — used when approved data for a major alteration is not associated with an STC.

=====================================================================
4. PRACTICAL COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST FOR AN APPLICANT
=====================================================================
[ ] A&P certificate in hand; both airframe and powerplant ratings currently effective; 3 years in effect documented.
[ ] 2 years of active engagement in maintaining 14 CFR-certificated aircraft documented immediately preceding application.
[ ] Fixed base of operations declared (address + telephone at which reachable during a normal working week); confirmed it need not be the place where IA authority is exercised.
[ ] Equipment, facilities, and current inspection data available at that base.
[ ] Application submitted on the form and in the manner prescribed by the Administrator (§ 65.91(a)).
[ ] Written test passed (major repairs, major alterations, annual and progressive inspections under Part 43). If failed, wait at least 90 days before reapplying for testing.
[ ] On the job: confirm Administrator-approved technical data exists BEFORE the alteration begins; inspect personally; check compatibility with prior repairs/alterations; make the § 43.9(d)/Appendix B record; keep the IA available for inspection and present it on request.

=====================================================================
5. CURRENCY AND WHAT I DID NOT VERIFY
=====================================================================
- Text quoted above is the eCFR 'current' text as retrieved 2026-11-15; confirm the in-force version at the date of use. Amendment history shown for § 65.91 ends at Amdt. 65-30, 50 FR 15700 (Apr. 19, 1985).
- NOT verified in this retrieval and therefore not stated as fact here: § 65.92 (duration of an inspection authorization) and § 65.93 (renewal) — verify directly before relying on renewal/currency details; and the formal definitions/classification of 'major alteration' in 14 CFR Part 1 (§ 1.1) and the major-alteration categories in Part 43 Appendix A. Those define WHAT a major alteration is; § 65.91 and § 65.95 define WHO may be qualified and privileged to act on one.
- § 65.91 does not itself prescribe who administers the written test beyond 'the Administrator'; confirm current FAA testing/administration procedure with the responsible Flight Standards office.

verdict.summary:
QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION (IA) AS THEY APPLY TO MAJOR ALTERATIONS — FAA / 14 CFR

=====================================================================
1. SHORT ANSWER
=====================================================================
The credential that authorizes a mechanic to inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft after a MAJOR ALTERATION is the Inspection Authorization issued under 14 CFR 65.91. The qualifications are the five eligibility elements of 14 CFR 65.91(c)(1)-(5):

  (1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with BOTH an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each currently effective and in effect for a total of at least 3 years;
  (2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before applying, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with 14 CFR Chapter I;
  (3) Have a fixed base of operations at which the applicant may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week (it need not be where the authority will be exercised);
  (4) Have available the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and
  (5) Pass a written test on the ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under Part 43.

Plus one procedural bar: an applicant who fails the (c)(5) test may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date of failure.

An A&P mechanic WITHOUT an IA cannot approve a major alteration for return to service in the Part 91 world: 65.85(a) and 65.87(a) both grant return-to-service authority only for maintenance or alteration "(excluding major repairs and major alterations)." The single narrow exception is the light-sport-category case in 65.85(b)/65.87(b).

=====================================================================
2. WHICH "INSPECTION AUTHORIZATION" — SCOPE OF THIS ANSWER
=====================================================================
"Inspection authorization" is read here as the Inspection Authorization (IA) rating issued under 14 CFR Part 65, Subpart D (65.91 eligibility; 65.93 renewal; 65.95 privileges and limitations). This is the only FAA credential denominated "inspection authorization," and it is the one that governs return to service after a major alteration.

If instead the question was meant as "what does a plain A&P need in order to sign off work," the answer is different and is given in section 5 below — a plain A&P cannot sign off a major alteration at all under Part 91 (except the LSA case). Both readings are covered so the answer holds either way.

=====================================================================
3. THE QUALIFICATIONS — VERBATIM REGULATORY TEXT (14 CFR 65.91)
=====================================================================
Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91 (fetched 2026-11-15T21:30:06Z; sha256 8dd2b52b76db)

"§ 65.91 Inspection authorization.

(a) An application for an inspection authorization is made on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator.

(b) An applicant who meets the requirements of this section is entitled to an inspection authorization.

(c) To be eligible for an inspection authorization, an applicant must—

(1) Hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both an airframe rating and a powerplant rating, each of which is currently effective and has been in effect for a total of at least 3 years;

(2) Have been actively engaged, for at least the 2-year period before the date he applies, in maintaining aircraft certificated and maintained in accordance with this chapter;

(3) Have a fixed base of operations at which he may be located in person or by telephone during a normal working week but it need not be the place where he will exercise his inspection authority;

(4) Have available to him the equipment, facilities, and inspection data necessary to properly inspect airframes, powerplants, propellers, or any related part or appliance; and

(5) Pass a written test on his ability to inspect according to safety standards for returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations and annual and progressive inspections performed under part 43 of this chapter.

An applicant who fails the test prescribed in paragraph (c)(5) of this section may not apply for retesting until at least 90 days after the date he failed the test."

Amendment history as published: Docket 1179, 27 FR 7973, Aug. 10, 1962, as amended by Amdt. 65-5, 31 FR 3337, Mar. 3, 1966; Amdt. 65-22, 42 FR 46279, Sept. 15, 1977; Amdt. 65-30, 50 FR 15700, Apr. 19, 1985. Note that 65.91 has not been amended since 1985, so the eligibility test above is stable and is the text currently on eCFR.

Element-by-element notes for an AMT applicant:

  (c)(1) — This is a certificate-currency test, not a school-diploma test. Both ratings must be on the certificate and currently effective, and the certificate must have been in effect at least 3 years. FAA-AMT training (Part 147 curriculum) satisfies the experience route to the A&P itself, but does not by itself satisfy (c)(1); the 3-year clock runs on the issued mechanic certificate.

  (c)(2) — Two years of ACTIVE engagement immediately preceding application, in maintaining aircraft that are certificated and maintained under 14 CFR Chapter I. "Actively engaged" is the operative phrase; it is an experience/recency test, not a training test.

  (c)(3) — A fixed base of operations where the applicant can be reached in person or by telephone during a normal working week. This base does not have to be where the IA authority is exercised.

  (c)(4) — Equipment, facilities, and inspection data must be actually available. For major alterations this is where the approved-data question bites (see section 6).

  (c)(5) — A written test, and the test content is expressly directed at "returning aircraft to service after major repairs and major alterations" and at annual/progressive inspections. Major alterations are a named subject of the IA test, which is why the IA is the correct answer to this question.

  Retest bar — 90 days after a failure. Do not conflate this 90-day figure with any other interval.

=====================================================================
4. PROCEDURAL / APPLICATION POINTS
=====================================================================
- Application is made "on a form and in a manner prescribed by the Administrator" (65.91(a)). The IA application is currently processed on FAA Form 8610-1 (Mechanic's Application for Inspection Authorization) through the responsible Flight Standards District Office / IAS; VERIFY the current form number and processing channel against FAA guidance before submitting, because form numbers and the processing system are administrative and change without a rule change.
- 65.91(b) is a mandatory-entitlement clause: an applicant who meets every element of 65.91(c) "is entitled to" the authorization. There is no discretionary approval step in the regulation text itself.

=====================================================================
5. WHY THE IA IS REQUIRED FOR MAJOR ALTERATIONS — THE CHAIN OF AUTHORITY
=====================================================================
(a) A&P privileges expressly exclude major alterations.
  14 CFR 65.85(a) (airframe rating): a certificated mechanic with an airframe rating may approve for return to service an airframe or related part or appliance after performing, supervising, or inspecting its maintenance or alteration "(excluding major repairs and major alterations)," and may perform and approve the Part 91 100-hour inspection.
  14 CFR 65.87(a) (powerplant rating): the identical structure for powerplants, propellers, and related parts or appliances, again "(excluding major repairs and major alterations)."
  Source: .../part-65/subpart-D/section-65.85 (fetched 2026-11-15T21:30:07Z; sha256 79dab817a228) and .../section-65.87 (fetched 2026-11-15T21:30:07Z; sha256 c1cba837bc02), both as amended by Docket FAA-2023-1377, Amdt. 65-66, 90 FR 35218 / 35219, July 24, 2025.

(b) The ONLY A&P-without-IA major-alteration path is the light-sport case.
  65.85(b) and 65.87(b) let an airframe- or powerplant-rated mechanic approve for return to service an airframe, powerplant, propeller, or related part/appliance of an aircraft with a special airworthiness certificate in the light-sport category, after performing and inspecting a major repair or major alteration, for products NOT produced under an FAA approval, and only where the alteration was authorized by and performed per instructions developed by the manufacturer or a person acceptable to the FAA. Outside that box, an A&P alone cannot sign off a major alteration.

(c) Return-to-service authority is routed through Part 65.
  14 CFR 43.7(a): except as provided in that section and 43.17, no person other than the Administrator may approve an aircraft, airframe, engine, propeller, appliance, or component part for return to service after maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, or alteration.
  43.7(b): "The holder of a mechanic certificate or an inspection authorization may approve ... for return to service as provided in Part 65 of this chapter." — i.e., 43.7 does not itself grant the authority; Part 65 defines its limits, and Part 65's limits exclude major alterations from plain A&P authority.
  43.7(c) repair station per Part 145; 43.7(d) manufacturer (but except for minor alterations the work must have been done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator); 43.7(e) Part 121/135 certificate holders per Part 121/135.
  Source: .../part-43/section-43.7 (fetched 2026-11-15T21:30:07Z; sha256 f177d9ffff23).

(d) Persons working under supervision are barred from the post-alteration inspection.
  14 CFR 43.3(d): a person working under the supervision of a mechanic or repairman certificate holder may perform the work the supervisor is authorized to perform, if personally observed and the supervisor is readily available in person — "However, this paragraph does not authorize the performance of any inspection required by Part 91 or Part 125 of this chapter or any inspection performed after a major repair or alteration."
  Source: .../part-43/section-43.3 (fetched 2026-11-15T21:30:07Z; sha256 b10f62b56b41).

So the answer to "who is qualified to inspect a major alteration" is: an IA holder (65.91), acting within 65.95, on work done to data approved by the Administrator — not an un-rated A&P and not a supervised helper.

=====================================================================
6. WHAT "QUALIFIED" MUST ALSO INCLUDE IN PRACTICE — DATA AND SCOPE
=====================================================================
- Approved data. A major alteration must be accomplished and signed off against technical data approved by the Administrator. 43.7(d) states the approved-data requirement expressly for manufacturer-approved return to service; the same requirement is carried into the IA's own privileges by 65.95 (see caveat in section 8). A holder of an IA who lacks the approved data for the specific alteration is not, in practice, in a position to approve it, and would also fail the 65.91(c)(4) "inspection data available" element.
- Major vs. minor. Whether an item is a major alteration is determined by 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix A (and 43.1(d)(3) carves Appendix A out for LSA products not produced under an FAA approval). Appendix A text was not part of the fetched grounding for this answer; cite it directly when classifying a specific alteration.
- Recording. Major repairs and alterations are recorded per Part 43 Appendix B and the FAA Form 337 requirement of 43.5. Neither Appendix B nor 43.5 was in the fetched grounding; cite directly.
- Applicability. 43.1(a) reaches aircraft with a U.S. airworthiness certificate; 43.1(b) excludes most experimental-certificate aircraft (with two stated exceptions) and Part 107 operations; 43.1(d) modifies applicability for light-sport category aircraft. Confirm the aircraft falls inside Part 43 before applying any of the above.

=====================================================================
7. CONTEXT THAT CHANGES THE ANSWER
=====================================================================
- Part 121 / 135 operator: 43.7(e) — the certificate holder approves return to service as provided in Part 121 or 135, so the operator's approved maintenance/inspection program, not the individual IA, may control the sign-off. The IA qualification question stays the same, but "who signs" may not be the IA.
- Part 145 repair station: 43.7(c) — return to service per Part 145, under the repair station certificate and its manual.
- Manufacturer: 43.7(d) — manufacturer may approve for return to service work it performed under 43.3(j), with approved technical data except for minor alterations.
- Light-sport category: 43.7(g) repairman certificate (light-sport aircraft) with a maintenance rating, plus the 65.85(b)/65.87(b) A&P exception described above.
- Experimental: 43.1(b) generally removes Part 43 applicability.

=====================================================================
8. CURRENCY AND SOURCES
=====================================================================
Primary source used: eCFR, Title 14, Chapter I, Subchapter C (Part 43) and Subchapter D (Part 65, Subpart D), as served at the URLs below and fetched 2026-11-15T21:30Z.
  - 14 CFR 65.91 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-65/subpart-D/section-65.91 (sha256 8dd2b52b76db)
  - 14 CFR 65.87 — .../section-65.87 (sha256 c1cba837bc02), Amdt. 65-66, 90 FR 35219, July 24, 2025
  - 14 CFR 65.85 — .../section-65.85 (sha256 79dab817a228), Amdt. 65-66, 90 FR 35218, July 24, 2025
  - 14 CFR 43.3 — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-14/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-43/section-43.3 (sha256 b10f62b56b41)
  - 14 CFR 43.7 — .../section-43.7 (sha256 f177d9ffff23)
  - 14 CFR 43.1 — .../section-43.1 (sha256 31b6a031254a), Amdt. 43-63, 90 FR 35211, July 24, 2025

The eCFR is authoritative as a current-text source but is not the official publication; the printed CFR and the Federal Register amendment are controlling in a dispute. Because 65.85 and 65.87 carry a July 24, 2025 amendment (light-sport provisions), re-verify before relying on the (b) paragraphs.

Adjacent sections NOT in the fetched grounding — read them directly before advising a client, and do not treat anything above as a paraphrase of them:
  - 14 CFR 65.93 — Inspection authorization: renewal (currency requirements; the activity/training renewal tests live here, not in 65.91).
  - 14 CFR 65.95 — Inspection authorization: privileges and limitations (the paragraph that authorizes an IA to inspect and approve for return to service after a major repair or major alteration done per Administrator-approved technical data, and the annual/progressive inspection authority, plus the continuous-airworthiness-maintenance-program carve-out).
  - 14 CFR 43.5 (Form 337), Part 43 Appendix A (major alteration list), Part 43 Appendix B (recordkeeping).
  - FAA guidance interpreting the above: the current FAA Order 8900.1 volume on maintenance, and the AC 65-series airworthiness/IA guidance.

=====================================================================
9. HOW TO VERIFY AN INDIVIDUAL'S IA QUALIFICATION (CHECKLIST)
=====================================================================
1. Mechanic certificate: airframe rating — currently effective? (65.91(c)(1))
2. Mechanic certificate: powerplant rating — currently effective? (65.91(c)(1))
3. Certificate in effect at least 3 years total? (65.91(c)(1))
4. Actively engaged in maintaining Chapter-I-certificated aircraft for at least the 2 years immediately before application? (65.91(c)(2))
5. Fixed base of operations with person-or-telephone reachability during a normal working week? (65.91(c)(3))
6. Equipment, facilities, and inspection data available for the article to be inspected? (65.91(c)(4)) — for a major alteration this means the Administrator-approved data for that specific alteration.
7. Written test passed; if previously failed, at least 90 days elapsed since the failure? (65.91(c)(5) and flush text)
8. IA currently effective (renewal per 65.93 — verify directly)?
9. Work to be approved is within 65.95 privileges, and the alteration is classified under Part 43 Appendix A as major?
10. Operating regime checked — Part 91 (IA signs) vs. Part 121/135 (43.7(e)) vs. Part 145 (43.7(c)) vs. manufacturer (43.7(d)) vs. LSA (65.85(b)/65.87(b), 43.7(g))?

If all of 1-9 are yes and step 10 resolves to Part 91, the individual is qualified to inspect and approve the major alteration for return to service.
